findings.description: STRONGEST: All three B-outputs pin a 'Quote Date' companion formula (`quote_date_formula`, tested in formula.rs's `positions_carries_a_locale_proof_quote_date_companion_column` and referenced in mapping.rs) as core, heavily-specified behavior of ticker resolution — exact constants: attribute literal `"tradetime"`, re-base by subtracting `DATE(1970,1,1)`, rendered via `TEXT(...,"0")`, wrapped in `IFERROR(...,"")`, and built from the SAME resolved ticker as the Price formula (same `resolve_ticker` call reused per row, per B1 'Both the Price and Quote Date cells shall be rendered as Cell::Formula'; B2 item 5; B3 E2/E3). The real EARS text for SHEET-MAP-001 says only: '...build the Price formula from the resolved ticker' — no mention of any second formula, any 'Quote Date' concept, or a same-ticker-reuse rule across columns. All 3 A-outputs (faithful to the given text) build only a single Price-formula function with no analog to Quote Date/tradetime whatsoever — confirming this is pure code-side surplus invisible from the spec text as given.

The `ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(Symbol)` defensive-error contract — one-row-per-symbol invariant, `Err` returned immediately on violation, `Display` output pinned to equal `Debug` (e.g. `DuplicateSymbolRow("AMZN")`) — is asserted by all 3 B-outputs as part of the ticker-mapping/row-rendering contract (B1 unwanted-behavior req; B2 point 7; B3 UB1/UB2), sourced from `render_positions`'s defensive `seen: BTreeSet<&Symbol>` guard and `tests/mapping.rs`'s `duplicate_symbol_guard_is_defensive...` test. SHEET-MAP-001's text says nothing about duplicate-row handling, error types, or row-identity invariants — it is scoped purely to resolve-then-build-Price-formula. Caveat: the code's own comment ties this guard to the same 'Symbol → Ticker Mapping' design section as the Price formula, so it may be governed by a sibling EARS ID (e.g. a SHEET-MAP-002) not shown in this audit's scope — but relative to the SHEET-MAP-001 text given, it is still surplus, and it shows B's code-blind reconstruction cannot distinguish EARS-ID boundaries within one design section.

Minor/expected surplus: all 3 B-outputs pin the exact Price-formula literal with no space after the comma — `=GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","price")` — and the rule that the ticker is embedded as a quoted literal 'never a cell reference' (B1, B2 point 4, B3 E1). SHEET-MAP-001 only says to 'build the Price formula from the resolved ticker,' leaving the exact formula syntax/spacing unstated. This is a natural, low-material necessity of any real implementation (something must be chosen) rather than a meaningful drift, but it is technically surplus versus the literal spec text.

Note (not scored as a finding per protocol — unanimous assumption with no spec-text basis): all 3 A-outputs invent that sheets-view itself owns the alias-map data structure and re-implements the identity-fallback logic locally (e.g. A1/A2's `SheetMapConfig.ticker_aliases: HashMap<Symbol,String>` with `.get(...).unwrap_or_else(identity)`; A3's `TickerAliases(HashMap<String,String>)`). The real code shows `sheets_view::resolve_ticker(aliases: &AliasMap, symbol: &str) -> String { aliases.resolve(symbol) }` is a bare one-line delegate — the alias map type (`config::AliasMap`) and its identity-fallback logic live entirely in the `config` crate, external to sheets-view. SHEET-MAP-001's phrasing ('via config's alias map (identity when unset)') is ambiguous about who implements the fallback, and all three A-runs independently guessed 'sheets-view does,' unanimously diverging from the real 'config does, sheets-view just delegates' answer. Per the classification rules this counts as an assumption artifact, not a scored A-finding, since it has no basis in explicit spec text either way — flagged here only as an interesting architecture-boundary ambiguity the spec leaves open, not as evidence for A-ONLY/BD drift.

notes: Direction A surfaced essentially no material spec-side surplus: nothing in the terse SHEET-MAP-001 text ('resolve Symbol to GOOGLEFINANCE ticker via config's alias map (identity when unset), build the Price formula from the resolved ticker') is dropped or under-implemented by the real code — the real resolve_ticker + price_formula fully honor it. All A-side divergences from the real code (Symbol modeled as a Hash/Eq newtype vs. the real Symbol being effectively a String/Deref<str> type consumed as &str; alias map owned locally vs. delegated to config::AliasMap; A3's defensive quote-escaping the real code lacks; A2/A3's extra space in the formula literal) are either unanimous inventions with no textual basis (assumption artifacts, per protocol) or single-run idiosyncrasies (A3's escaping), not spec-text-traceable gaps. Direction B, by contrast, converged tightly (all 3 runs, near-verbatim) on a large block of code+test-enforced behavior entirely outside SHEET-MAP-001's stated scope: the Quote Date companion formula and its exact constants, the same-ticker-reuse-per-row rule, and the DuplicateSymbolRow defensive contract. Because A shows no comparable spec-side surplus to pair with this, the relationship is B-ONLY-DRIFT rather than BD-DRIFT: the code's 'Symbol → Ticker Mapping' section is doing substantially more than SHEET-MAP-001 alone documents, but nothing SHEET-MAP-001 documents is missing from the code. Worth flagging to the requirements author: either SHEET-MAP-001 needs a sibling EARS ID (e.g. SHEET-MAP-002) to own the Quote Date formula and the duplicate-row guard explicitly, or SHEET-MAP-001 itself should be broadened to state them, since a cold reader of only the given EARS text would never anticipate that resolving a ticker also gates a second locale-proof date formula and a loud-error invariant.
